prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
It’s time for real change. Labour’s 2019 manifesto offers a transformative programme to rebuild Britain for the many, not the few—ending a decade of austerity, tackling the climate emergency, reversing falling living standards and putting wealth and power in democratic hands.

Labour will rewrite the rules of the economy with a £400bn National Transformation Fund (including a £250bn Green Transformation Fund), a National Investment Bank and Regional Development Banks, and a crackdown on tax avoidance. Those earning over £80,000 and big corporations will pay a little more; no rise in VAT. Public money will serve public goals.

A Green Industrial Revolution will deliver most emissions cuts by 2030, create one million good, unionised jobs and cut bills. Labour will ban fracking; build massive new wind and solar capacity; back new nuclear for security; retrofit almost all homes; expand storage and grids; trial tidal and green hydrogen; and permanently prioritise nature recovery. Energy and water will be brought into democratic public ownership to accelerate decarbonisation, end profiteering and cut fuel poverty. A windfall tax will make oil giants pay their share.

Work will pay and be secure: a Real Living Wage of at least £10 for all over 16; day‑one rights; a ban on zero‑hours contracts; sectoral collective bargaining; union freedoms restored; and a gradual move to a 32‑hour average full‑time week with no loss of pay, funded by productivity gains.

Universal, world‑class public services will be rebuilt. The NHS will receive average 4.3% annual funding rises; privatisation will end; free prescriptions and basic dentistry will be introduced; mental health services modernised; and social care transformed into a National Care Service with free personal care, ethical provision and better pay and conditions for carers. A National Education Service will provide free lifelong learning—from Sure Start Plus and 30 hours’ free preschool for all 2–4‑year‑olds, to free further/higher education, restored maintenance grants, well‑funded schools, smaller classes, an Arts Premium and an end to high‑stakes SATs; academies and free schools will return to democratic oversight.

Transport will be a clean public service: rail and buses brought into public ownership; 3,000 lost bus routes restored; free bus travel for under‑25s where councils run services; nationwide electrification; HS2 to Scotland; Crossrail for the North; safer walking/cycling; and a 2030 phase‑out target for new combustion‑engine car sales, backed by charging roll‑out. Free full‑fibre broadband will be delivered by a publicly owned British Broadband.

Housing is a right: over one million new council and social homes in a decade; end Right to Buy; zero‑carbon standards; rent controls; open‑ended tenancies and an end to no‑fault evictions; leasehold scandal abolished; rough sleeping ended within five years.

Justice and security will be rooted in prevention, rights and accountability: rebuild neighbourhood policing and youth services; restore legal aid; reunify probation; tackle violence against women and girls; adopt a health‑led approach to substance misuse. Defence will remain committed to NATO and the renewal of Trident, with proper pay, housing and support for forces and veterans, and a strategy aligned with climate goals.

Labour will end the hostile environment, scrap the 2014 Immigration Act, end indefinite detention and uphold family life and safe routes for refugees. Social security will be rebuilt with dignity: Universal Credit scrapped, sanctions ended, the benefit cap and two‑child limit abolished, and disability and carer support improved. A Right to Food will halve food bank use within a year.

Democracy will be renewed: an elected Senate to replace the Lords via a Constitutional Convention; votes at 16; automatic voter registration; dark money and lobbying curbed; second jobs for MPs ended; FOI extended. Brexit will be settled by a final‑say referendum within six months—between a new, worker‑ and climate‑protecting deal (customs union, close Single Market alignment) and remain—and Labour will implement the result. Internationally, Labour will pursue peace, human rights and climate justice: a War Powers Act; suspend arms sales used in abuses (e.g., Yemen, Palestine) and recognise Palestine; restore climate diplomacy; keep aid at 0.7% focused on reducing inequality.

The future is ours to make. For the many, not the few.
